fixes.explanation: Noon is a fine time for a lot of jobs, baker, but it's not the one the text gives. Aaron tends the lamps "…from evening until morning." (Leviticus 24:3). That's the stretch the LORD names, and noon isn't in it.

I see why you'd pick a place for offerings, baker, but that's not where these loaves go. The LORD says to set them "…on the table of pure gold before the LORD." (Leviticus 24:6). A gold table, with the loaves in two rows, six per row. That's the spot.
That's the one. "Every Sabbath day the bread is to be set out before the LORD…" (Leviticus 24:8). So the setting out happens on the Sabbath, week after week. I love a good schedule, baker.

Foreigners is a fair guess, baker, but they're not named in this verse. The bread is set out "…on behalf of the Israelites as a permanent covenant." (Leviticus 24:8). The Israelites are the ones the text names. I once watched the mystery key, a friend from the drawer I lived in, guess at doors all day long. Guessing is how we all learn.

That's a generous idea, baker, but the verse names someone else. The bread "…belongs to Aaron and his sons, who are to eat it in a holy place…" (Leviticus 24:9). They're the ones who get it. Nice thought, though.

False is right. Aaron and his sons "…are to eat it in a holy place…" (Leviticus 24:9). So the verse doesn't say "anywhere they like." It names a holy place. The text calls the bread "…a most holy part of the food offerings to the LORD…" and I think that's why the place matters.
